videos.script: Every CSS rule has two halves. A selector, which picks elements. And declarations, which say what to do to them. {{rule}} This lesson is mostly about the first half, and about one question. {{conflict}} On a real site, many rules pick the same element. One says this paragraph is grey. Another says paragraphs in an event are green. A third says notes are brown. The browser has to choose one colour. {{cascade}} The way it chooses is called the cascade. It is not a guess, and it is not the last rule in the file. It is a fixed list of questions, asked in order. Where does the rule come from. Is it important. How specific is its selector. And only then, which one came last. {{specificity}} Specificity is the part people find hardest, so you will count it. Ids, then classes, then element names, as three numbers. {{inherit}} Some properties are not set on an element at all. They come down from its parent. Colour and fonts do this. Borders and margins do not. {{devtools}} And at the end, the tool that ends every argument about CSS. DevTools lists every rule that matched, in order, with the losers crossed out. You will read that list for each case in this lesson. {{end}}
